objective: Provide a provider-neutral, durable, capability-scoped handoff lease that separates proposal, approval, and consumption for autonomous multi-agent execution.

research.conclusion: The current Agents SDK documentation emphasizes agents, handoffs, agents-as-tools, guardrails, approvals, sessions, sandbox workspaces, tracing, and resumable state.
research.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds explicit proposal/approval/consume transitions and generation-fenced resumability without depending on a provider SDK.

research.conclusion: The SDK exposes handoffs, guardrails, sessions, MCP tool calling, sandbox capabilities, tracing, and resumable run state as composable agent-runtime primitives.
research.implementation_impact: FAISAL records handoff ownership, capability masks, expiry, approval evidence, and consume receipts as auditable control-plane state.

research.conclusion: MCP defines capability negotiation, asynchronous Tasks, Skills-over-MCP, progress, cancellation, and explicit trust/safety requirements; tool descriptions and annotations are not automatically authority.
research.implementation_impact: The lease treats model output, MCP metadata, tool descriptions, and external content as untrusted data and requires explicit capability and approval checks before consumption.

research.conclusion: MCP Skills are portable instruction sets with progressive discovery and explicit deployment/auth/tool-design decisions.
research.implementation_impact: Skill- or MCP-originated handoff proposals must still pass the same lease state machine and cannot self-authorize capabilities or irreversible actions.

research.conclusion: The live provider model catalog remains a changing capability/cost metadata source and is not privileged authority.
research.implementation_impact: The handoff contract contains no hard-coded provider/model privilege and records provider metadata only outside the authorization boundary.

features: proposal, approval, consume, revoke, and expiry state machine
explicit approval policy and approval digest
SHA-256 lease, record, continuity, and receipt digests
model-proposal, verified-context, and operator-approval provenance flags
implementation.state_machine: PROPOSED -> APPROVED -> CONSUMED; PROPOSED/APPROVED -> REVOKED or EXPIRED

validation.selftest: FHL_HANDOFF_LEASE_SELFTEST_OK cases=31 consumed=2 expired=1 revoked=1 replay=verified

benchmark.interpretation: The durable handoff lease is intentionally slower than the prior in-memory coordination microbenchmark because every transition is journaled and fsynced. The result measures durability overhead and is not a claim of end-to-end agent latency or throughput superiority.

adjacent_regressions.m223_inference_contract: FIC_SELFTEST_EXIT=0; fixture repaired to seed request_sequence and deterministic logical now_ns

live_model_catalog.interpretation: The catalog was researched for provider-neutral adapter and routing design only. No model output, model ID, price, or provider metadata grants authority.

qualification_limits: The handoff lease is a bounded userspace/control-plane primitive and does not replace the existing coordination, task, agent-runtime, capability, safety, or distributed replication services.

The durable benchmark is intentionally not compared as if it were equivalent to the prior in-memory coordination benchmark; fsync durability adds substantial overhead and the measurements are reported separately.
No live paid-model call, MCP server, browser session, robotics device, physical accelerator, production cluster, or operator approval ceremony was used.

The legacy model-orchestration wrapper remains intentionally blocked by the repository’s unqualified-legacy guard; current M223, M230, M236, and M241 validations passed and are the valid adjacent paths.
Production approval remains blocked by the existing external builder, signing, physical hardware, secure boot/TPM, live multihost, independent security review, and CVE-ownership requirements.
